I'll work through this carefully, comparing source and draft passage by passage.

**Opening fog paragraph:** The draft omits the detail about the Greenwich pensioners "wheezing by the firesides of their wards" and the skipper being "down in his close cabin." These are atmospheric details but not signature-level.

**Temple Bar passage:** Source has "the dense fog is densest" — draft has "the dense fog densest" (missing "is"). Minor.

**"who made a fortune by it":** Source says solicitors "some two or three of whom have inherited it from their fathers, who made a fortune by it" — the draft omits "who made a fortune by it." This is an interpretively significant satirical detail.

**"In trickery, evasion...":** Source has "In trickery, evasion, procrastination, spoliation, botheration, under false pretences of all sorts, there are influences that can never come to good." The draft flattens this to "Trickery, evasion...never come to good" — losing the rhetorical force of "there are influences."

**"shirking and sharking":** Source: "Shirking and sharking in all their many varieties have been sown broadcast by the ill-fated cause." Draft: "shirkings and sharkings have been sown broadcast" — minor variation.

**"really will come to a settlement one of these days":** Source includes "and really will come to a settlement one of these days" — the ironic coda to the costs question. The draft drops "and really will come to a settlement one of these days." This is a signature ironic aside.

**The prisoner presentation scene:** Source has a fuller paragraph: "The Chancellor is about to bow to the bar when the prisoner is presented. Nothing can possibly come of the prisoner's conglomeration but his being sent back to prison, which is soon done. The man from Shropshire ventures another remonstrative 'My lord!'" — the draft collapses this significantly.

The most significant losses are the ironic "really will come to a settlement one of these days" and the "who made a fortune by it" — both carrying interpretive/satirical weight. Most other material is faithfully preserved or only mildly compressed.
